text:
lina: new thought: build a lightweight "credential ambassador" focused only on minting short-lived, route-scoped creds for cross-project calls. it would NOT proxy payloads, just issue tokens after attestation.

mike: sounds promising. biggest difference vs broker/proxy is no payload hop, right? what about token shape and how downstream validates?

lina: correct, direct traffic. idea: ambassador issues opaque tokens by default + an introspect endpoint. optional signed compact claim blob (sig-v1) for low-cost validation without introspect.

sasha: opaque w/ introspect reduces token leak surface. downside is extra roundtrip for downstreams that can't afford introspect latency. compact claims help but need fast rotation.

jordana: multi-tenant isolation is key. ambassador must shard keys by org (or per-tenant ambassador instances). no global key that mints across tenants. also strict ACLs per-route.

mike: threat model: if ambassador key is compromised, attacker mints tokens. mitigations? HSM-backed keys, per-ambassador KMS partitions, very short TTLs, and active rotation.

lina: agreed. TTL proposal: 20s-120s depending on route latency profile. high-throughput internal-only routes could be longer (up to 5m) with additional protections.

sasha: telemetry: each minted token should carry a lineage id: requester principal, caller IP, request-id, route-intent. ambassador logs must have signed, append-only shards for audit.

jordana: operationally, ambassador outage affects minters. fallback patterns: client-side cache with jitter; prefetch for hot flows; fallback to legacy service-account token for critical tenants. document these fallbacks.

mike: rate limiting: per-caller and per-tenant mint quotas. tie into alerting when abnormal mint patterns occur. also billing signals for heavy minters.

lina: attestation for mint: mTLS client cert, or signed request from caller (operator token). ambassador must validate identity and map to principal. ambassador should NOT mint tokens that impersonate arbitrary operators w/o proof.

sasha: authorization model: ambassador is NOT the final authorizer. downstream services must still perform RBAC. ambassador tokens express identity+intent only. keep authz central.

jordana: migration plan: 1) internal infra-only pilot, 2) integrate SDK flag to request via ambassador, 3) cross-team pilot for non-critical routes, 4) evaluate metrics (mint latency, introspect p50/p95, failure rate, cache miss rate) for 2w, 5) wider rollout.

mike: metrics to track: token_mint_latency_ms, token_mint_errors, introspect_latency_ms, token_revocations, mint_rate_per_tenant. also SLO for mint endpoint (p95 < 50ms?).

lina: headers we expect downstream to accept by default:

    Authorization: Bearer <ambassador-ephemeral>
    X-Amba-Req-Id: <uuid>
    X-Amba-Proto: sig-v1 | opaque

mike: minor impl detail: provide a small introspect cache for downstreams to avoid hitting authz every request when using opaque tokens. TTL keyed by token id.

sasha: security extras: mint signing keys in KMS with rotation policy, split engineers for key ops, require U2F/okta for any key material ops. consider attested hardware for ambassador infra.

jordana: logging + privacy: tokens should not leak PII. ensure lineage data in logs is redacted by default and can be unredacted under audit.

ops-bot: reminder: create runbook for ambassador error modes (unavailable, high-error, slow-introspect). add oncall rotation and escalation.

lina: i'll draft a short RFC with diagrams (caller->ambassador->introspect->target), TTL suggestions, rate limits, migration steps and an operations checklist. @mike @jordana please review before i post.

mike: will look this afternoon.

jordana: can do EOD.

sasha: will add a security checklist comment after reading.
